title: astripomoea grantii
intro: Astripomoea grantii, commonly known as the "Bushman's poison" or "African poison bulb", is a plant species within the family Convolvulaceae. It is used in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including fever, rheumatism, and snake bites. The plant is said to have health benefits such as reducing inflammation and acting as an antibacterial agent, which may be attributed to its therapeutic actions of analgesia and anti-inflammatory effects. The bioactive constituents of Astripomoea grantii include alkaloids, glycosides, and other compounds that contribute to its medicinal properties.
